summary: Kashan Airport is a domestic airport serving the historic city of Kashan in Isfahan Province, Iran, located on the edge of the Dasht-e Kavir desert region. It functions as a convenient gateway for travelers visiting Kashan's renowned UNESCO-registered Fin Garden, traditional merchant houses, and the ancient Sialk archaeological site. The airport handles a modest volume of regional flights, making it a popular entry point for cultural tourism in central Iran.
faqs:
Q: Does Kashan Airport have international flights?
A: No, Kashan Airport primarily serves domestic routes, with flights connecting to major Iranian cities such as Tehran and Mashhad.

Q: How far is the airport from Kashan city center?
A: The airport is located roughly 10-15 kilometers south of the city center, typically a 20-30 minute drive depending on traffic.

Q: Are there facilities for overnight stays at the airport?
A: The airport has basic terminal amenities, but most travelers prefer hotels in Kashan city, which range from restored traditional houses to modern options.

Q: Can I catch a direct flight to other tourist destinations?
A: Direct flights from Kashan are limited; many visitors transit through Tehran's airports for connections to other parts of Iran or abroad.
transport_tips: Taxis and ride services are the most common way to reach the city from Kashan Airport, as there is no rail link or extensive public bus service. Pre-arranging a hotel pickup or hiring a driver familiar with Kashan's tourist sites is recommended, especially for first-time visitors. Car rentals are available in Kashan city rather than at the airport itself, so plan accordingly if you intend to drive yourself.
local_tip: Time your visit to coincide with the annual rosewater harvesting festival in spring (late April to mid-May), when the nearby Qamsar and Niasar regions transform into fragrant celebrations—your hotel in Kashan can help arrange guided tours to the rose fields.
